identity.name: BLUESTONE JEWEL LFSTL LTD
identity.industry: Consumer Discretionary / Branded Omnichannel Jewellery (design-led, online-origin)

summary.oneLiner: BlueStone is a digital-first, vertically integrated fine jewellery brand building for India's everyday/daily-wear jewellery consumer through an omnichannel network of stores and its online platform.
summary.business: BlueStone designs, manufactures (over 95% of jewellery in-house) and retails fine jewellery in India through an omnichannel model combining physical stores, which act as trust anchors, with a digital-first platform that drives discovery and demand generation. The company positions itself around daily-wear/'everyday luxury' consumption rather than only occasion-led (wedding/festival) jewellery purchases, and has grown from a digital-first start-up in 2011 to 340 stores across 134 cities.

endMarkets: India - domestic jewellery retail, omnichannel across Tier 1/2/3 cities (340 stores across 134 cities)

currentContext.strengths: High vertical integration - over 95% of jewellery manufactured in-house, enabling faster design-to-market cycles, responsiveness to demand shifts and control over quality|Digital-first discovery engine - nearly 300 million online sessions in the year used as a demand-signal/design feedback loop feeding in-house manufacturing and omnichannel selling|High repeat-purchase base - 54.5% of FY26 revenue came from repeat customers, indicating loyalty/brand trust versus one-off occasion purchases|Store-maturity compounding - older stores show improving economics over time as local brand recognition and repeat custom build, distinct from occasion-led retail formats|Highest revenue growth among leading jewellery retail peers in the period while maintaining gross margins
currentContext.strategies: The ultimate consumer partnership - become the most trusted jewellery partner for the modern Indian consumer across every life stage and occasion, moving beyond purely occasion-led buying|Leadership through design innovation - lead a 'design revolution' via a portfolio spanning daily wear, occasion-led and statement pieces, investing in design capability and faster product development cycles|Expanding nationwide access and scale - significantly expand physical footprint with a disciplined, data-led approach, targeting a network of 700+ stores over the long term across metros and emerging cities|Technology as a force multiplier - embed AI/analytics and unified digital systems across design, manufacturing, inventory management and consumer engagement (rather than layering technology on top) to enable scale and responsiveness|Building a professionally managed organisation - strengthen organisational and management capability as part of the FY30 strategic blueprint|Driving sustainable value creation - deliver enduring value for consumers and shareholders as part of the FY30 strategic blueprint|The Company maintains a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (per SEBI LODR Regulation 43A) governing declaration and pay-out of dividend. The policy distinguishes interim dividend (which the Board may declare at its discretion during the year, typically after quarterly/half-yearly financials) from final dividend (recommended at the time of approving the Annual Financial Statements), with the Board weighing all relevant factors in shareholders' best interest before recommending any pay-out versus retaining profits.
currentContext.expansion: BlueStone is an asset-light omnichannel jewellery retailer expanding via store network additions rather than manufacturing capacity build-out. The distribution footprint expanded to 340 stores across 134 cities as at 31 March 2026, with 65 new store additions during the year, balanced between new and existing geographies and between mall and high-street formats; more than half of the store network is less than three years old, which management flags as a structural tailwind as these stores mature. During the year the Company also opened two dedicated stores in the Men's and Kids category, a largely underserved format it intends to continue expanding. For FY27, management has flagged plans to significantly increase the retail footprint further, with a strategic focus on driving both store density in existing markets and geographic expansion across city tiers.
currentContext.mdna: India's 'Consumer Renaissance' - a demographic and social shift from large joint-family, price-sensitive, unorganised buying toward nuclear-family, convenience-led, organised-retail/e-commerce consumption, with rising female workforce participation and urban sprawl into Tier 2/3 cities - underpins domestic consumption demand|India's e-commerce market is expected to expand at a 20-25% CAGR through 2029, with digital channels shifting from a transactional medium to the primary point of product discovery, favouring digital-first, omnichannel brands|The Indian jewellery sector is shifting structurally from an occasional, wedding-led, pure-gold purchase pattern toward a 'lifestyle consumer' pattern with daily-wear, diamond and studded/14k-18k gold demand growing faster than wedding-led gold demand|Southern India remains the largest regional demand pocket (41% of demand, plain-gold/temple designs) while Northern and Western India show higher propensity for lightweight studded jewellery, and daily-wear/occasion-led demand is rising across all regions|Rising disposable incomes and urbanisation in Tier 2/Tier 3+ cities are converting a still largely unorganised jewellery/general-trade market (82% unorganised) toward organised, value-added retail channels|Company-specific: a sharp, unprecedented rise in gold prices during the year caused the demand-driven inventory system to unintentionally thin out entry-level/affordable price points, weighing on new-consumer acquisition before the entry-level portfolio was redesigned and growth recovered above 30% by Q4 exit

risks.risk: Commodity price fluctuations in gold and diamonds
risks.note: Cost structure is highly sensitive to global precious-metal/gemstone prices; sharp volatility impacts consumer affordability (postponed/cancelled purchases, trade-down to lighter pieces), raises working-capital needs and can compress margins.

Operational efficiency depends on consistent availability of high-quality gold, diamonds and gemstones and on certain manufacturing processes; disruption or quality deterioration could delay production and affect customer satisfaction.

Aggressive expansion and pricing/promotions from national jewellery chains, regional players and emerging D2C entrants can escalate customer acquisition costs and pressure profitability and market share.
The jewellery sector faces frequent shifts in import duties, mandatory hallmarking, foreign trade policy and GST structures, which can abruptly alter cost bases and require pricing-strategy changes.

Jewellery consumption is concentrated around festive and wedding seasons in India, creating revenue/demand concentration risk that the company is trying to offset via non-seasonal 'Everyday Wear' and gifting collections.

A large digital/omnichannel footprint means the company handles significant volumes of customer data and financial transactions; a breach could cause operational disruption, legal liability and reputational damage.

Inflation spikes, currency depreciation or geopolitical disruptions can weaken consumer sentiment for a high-value discretionary category like jewellery, and high interest rates raise financing costs for both the company and consumers.

risks.risk: Evolving fashion trends and new materials
risks.note: The industry must keep pace with fast-changing global/regional fashion trends and adoption of new materials such as lab-grown diamonds (LGDs); failure to refresh the catalogue in time could affect sales and growth.

one-line thesis: Revenue **+49% to ₹733cr** with pre-Ind-AS EBITDA **+135% to ₹55cr** (7.5% margin, +273bps) — the whole argument of this call is that the cost base is growing far slower than revenue, and that the operating leverage sits at the **corporate/marketing level, not the store level**. SSSG of 39% was broad-based with older cohorts in line with the portfolio. The stress point management was pressed on all call: **new-customer adds slipped from ~50k to ~40k a quarter** because of merchandise dislocation at entry price points during the gold spike, and the ₹12,000cr-in-four-years target rests on "long-term SSSG" arithmetic that is explicitly *not* the reported SSSG.
financial scorecard (q1 fy27):
| Metric | Q1FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | **₹733cr** | **+49%** | against a 6%→15% customs-duty hike on gold mid-quarter |
| EBITDA (pre-Ind AS) / margin | **₹55cr · 7.5%** | **+135%**, margin **+273bps** | ~3x the rate of revenue growth |
| PAT (rptd & normalized) | not disclosed on call | — | — |
| Gross margin | **+100bps** ex-inventory gain | — | CFO discouraged reading it — product/studded mix noise; **contribution margin is the right metric and is "largely stable"** |
| SSSG | **39%** | broad-based | older cohorts posting SSSG in line with the overall portfolio |
| Store count | **352 stores** | — | Q1 additions "softer"; ~4,500 sq ft new-store size |
| Studded mix | **57%** | — | |
| AOV | **~₹78,000** | — | repeat AOV runs **20–30% higher** than new |
| Inventory | **₹2,800cr** (vs ₹2,650cr in March) | — | analyst's "up ₹600–700cr" was corrected on the call |
| Marketing spend | **₹50cr · 6.9%** of revenue | flat as % (6.9% LY) | FY26 full-year was 6.6%, down from ~9.2% four years ago |
| Repeat revenue share | **60%** | **+9pp** | ~1mn-customer base, ageing |
| New customers added | **~40,000** | down from ~50,000/qtr | the acknowledged soft spot |
| Manufacturing | **~95% in-house** | — | worth a **300–400bps** margin delta vs 50–60% outsourcers, but framed as strategic not cost-driven |
> Adjustments / one-offs: gross margin quoted **excluding inventory gain**; management explicitly warned against reading quarterly gross-margin or marketing-% moves. Demand softened in May post duty hike, normalised through June, and July is tracking "no major difference compared to what we observed in June."
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue: ~₹12,000cr in the next four years** (from ₹2,440cr in FY26) — the anchor number, restated three times.
- **SSSG ~30% over the next four years** — but critically, this is **"SSSG even at maturity," not reported SSSG**; reported SSSG will run higher because of first-year stores on a low base. Management conceded the analyst's arithmetic that 30% SSSG + 20% distribution ≠ 50% revenue CAGR on a reported basis.
- **Distribution growth ~20% CAGR (store count) over four years**, to be delivered through this year as well — store adds should **not** be read linearly quarter to quarter.
- **Operating EBITDA margin: 7.5% → "the 15% handle" over the next four years**, with the *bigger chunk* of that coming from **scale (marketing + corporate cost dilution), not store-level profitability**.
- **Marketing spend: 6.6% (FY26) → ~4.5–4.6% over the next five years**; this full year should print **below 6.6%**.
- **Blended inventory turn → ~1.7–1.8** over the next four years; "this year inventory turn should get better," improving each year.
- **Store-level ROIC ~40%** at mature inventory turns — already demonstrated by older stores, which are *still* delivering SSSG in line with or better than company average.
- **Hedge policy unchanged: ~50% of gold inventory hedged** (GML included as a hedging instrument); explicitly **not** a function of the gold price view.
- No 9-karat launch planned currently; 14-karat experiments continue at lower price points.
order book & pipeline: Not applicable (retail). The pipeline proxy is the store network — 352 stores, ~20% p.a. distribution CAGR, larger (~4,500 sq ft) formats in Tier-2/3 where rent per sq ft is lower, giving greater frontage at similar absolute rent per store.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Channel is deliberately not segmented**: **>80% of sales originate online**, but the store is where trust is sealed. Management insists these are one continuous journey, and that store productivity is higher than a pure physical retailer's *because* intent is built online first.
- **Product**: studded 57%; entry-price-point recalibration via redesign (new techniques giving more strength with less gold) plus selective 14-karat, not karatage alone.
- **Manufacturing**: ~95% in-house. The stated rationale is **design defensibility, not margin** — in a vendor ecosystem "your designs eventually get dissipated, get commoditized, get stocked with small tweaks in different stores across different brands."
- **Lab-grown diamonds: a non-event for this business.** Solitaire exposure (where LGD actually competes) is **<1% of revenue**, so BlueStone "never saw the first shift or the second shift."
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Customer ageing as the growth engine**: acquisition happens at age 28–32 at low ticket; the same customer at 45–50 buys ₹4–6 lakh products. The stated corollary is that BlueStone must **grow its selection upward as the base ages** — repeat AOV is already 20–30% above new.
- **Tier-2/3 densification** with larger-frontage stores at comparable absolute rent, used partly as billboard/advertising surface.
- **Non-wedding everyday jewellery** — framed as the segment "the industry overlooked for a very long time" and the deliberate positioning choice.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Design-first + full in-house tech stack** — "the only jewellery company that has built its entire technology stack in-house"; 95% in-house manufacturing exists to stop design leakage, which is what sustains premium pricing.
- **Cohort compounding**: stores at **~40% store-level ROIC are still posting SSSG in line with or better than company average** — i.e. maturity has not capped growth, which is the specific evidence for the four-year math.
- **Consumer-internet metric set** (cohorts, repeat share, wallet share, customer lifetime) applied to a category that historically ran on relationships and brand marketing.
- **~1mn customer base, ageing into higher ticket sizes** — a compounding annuity that competitors cannot buy.
margins & cost dynamics:
- The margin story is deliberately relocated: **do not look at gross margin** (product-mix noise), **look at contribution margin** (captures cost of production/manufacturing and direct costs) — which is "reasonably stable" — **and then at operating leverage**.
- Of the ~650bps of operating-leverage expansion in the last year, **the bigger chunk came from scale (corporate + marketing dilution), not store-level profit expansion**. Management used this to rebut the suggestion that slower expansion would deliver margin sooner: "that base assumption itself is flawed."
- Rent grew 35% vs 25.5% area growth; management's answer is that per-store economics (absolute rent, revenue, cost per store) are the right unit and are stable — larger Tier-2/3 stores are not "operational square feet," and lease escalation is **3–5% p.a.**
- **GMROI has declined from ~62% (FY23) to ~48% (FY26)** — management's explanation is mathematical, not structural: heavy new-store addition (young cohorts dilute turns) plus gold-price inflation on the balance-sheet date. Mature cohorts already run **1.8–2.0x** inventory turns.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- Store adds were **softer this quarter**; management refused to give a linear run-rate and reaffirmed the **~20% distribution CAGR** for the year.
- New stores ~4,500 sq ft; no material change in investment per store — larger frontage obtained at similar cost in Tier-2/3.
capital allocation:
- **Hedging is a risk-management policy, not a view**: ~50% of gold inventory hedged, designed around liquidity, capital structure and P&L impact. Unchanged despite gold stabilising. GML counts within the 50%.
- Inventory ₹2,800cr is the dominant capital deployment; the stated path to better ROCE runs through **inventory turn improving to 1.7–1.8** as the store base ages, not through inventory reduction.
- Marketing spend rises in absolute terms every year but falls as a % of revenue — an explicit, ongoing reallocation toward market share.
risks & watch-items:
1. **New-customer additions fell to ~40k/qtr from ~50k** — the merchandise dislocation at entry price points was "real." Management says month-on-month trends have ticked up over the last 3–4 months, but the YoY comparison is still negative. **This is the number to watch.**
2. **Growth is increasingly repeat-led** (60% of revenue, +9pp). Healthy while the base ages, but it masks weak top-of-funnel if new adds don't recover.
3. **The ₹12,000cr / 50% CAGR math depends on "long-term SSSG," not reported SSSG** — management conceded the reported-number arithmetic doesn't work. This is a real disclosure-quality risk if cohorts decelerate.
4. **Gold-price volatility is the dominant external variable** — and, counter-intuitively, *rising* gold hurts this business (merchandise dislocation in real time). Q3 last year, the sharpest gold rise, was "the slowest quarter in our history."
5. **Customs duty 6% → 15%** softened May demand; the durable effect is unresolved and gold exchange volumes are structurally higher this year.
6. **GMROI compression** — explained mathematically, but it is a four-year decline and only reverses if the promised turn improvement lands.
7. **Disclosure gaps**: inventory in kg refused as competitive; no target new-customer number; no repeat-AOV split by tier or quarter.
management quality / tone: Conviction-heavy and framework-driven; Kushwaha reframes the company as "a consumer internet company that has chosen jewellery as its category" and pushes analysts to look forward rather than back. Two moments stand out as credibility-positive: he **conceded outright** that the 50%-CAGR arithmetic doesn't work on reported SSSG ("you are absolutely right, that's not the way the numbers add up") rather than defending it, and he **corrected an analyst's inventory error with the actual March base** instead of letting it stand. Against that, several micro-questions (ideal new-customer growth, repeat AOV split, inventory in kg, tier-wise AOV) were declined as "too micro" or "too competitive" — the disclosure floor here is noticeably higher-level than peers'.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **Rising gold is a headwind, not a tailwind, for this model.** The customer is a *price-point* buyer (₹20–40k), not a grammage buyer — so gold inflation shrinks the assortment available at the customer's fixed budget rather than lifting ticket size. Investment-led demand (gold coins) is explicitly not their customer.
- **The operating leverage is corporate, not store-level.** This inverts the usual retail intuition and is why management wants *faster* not slower expansion — slowing down would delay, not accelerate, the path from 7.5% to 15%.
- **Lab-grown diamonds were always noise for BlueStone** because the disruption happened in large solitaires, <1% of their revenue. "We never saw the first shift or the second shift."
- **GMROI decline is a mix artefact of rapid store addition** — the dilution from new stores shrinks as the base grows, so the reported turn should mechanically improve from here even with no change in underlying store performance.
- Store-level ROIC of ~40% in mature cohorts **with SSSG still at or above company average** is the single most load-bearing datapoint for the four-year target; it is the thing to falsify.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: BlueStone is a digital-first, vertically integrated fine jewellery brand building for India's everyday/daily-wear jewellery consumer through an omnichannel network of stores and its online platform.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: BlueStone designs, manufactures (over 95% of jewellery in-house) and retails fine jewellery in India through an omnichannel model combining physical stores, which act as trust anchors, with a digital-first platform that drives discovery and demand generation. The company positions itself around daily-wear/'everyday luxury' consumption rather than only occasion-led (wedding/festival) jewellery purchases, and has grown from a digital-first start-up in 2011 to 340 stores across 134 cities.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Ethereal House Private Limited — subsidiary: Became a subsidiary under a shareholders' agreement dated 6 January 2025 (shares allotted 13 January 2025); Company holds 75.51% on a diluted basis (excluding ESOP pool).
- Redefine Fashion Private Limited — associate: Associate under a shareholders' agreement dated 11 November 2024 (shares allotted 15 November 2024); Company holds equity shares and CCPS representing 49.12% on a diluted basis (excluding ESOP pool).

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Channel is deliberately not segmented**: **>80% of sales originate online**, but the store is where trust is sealed. Management insists these are one continuous journey, and that store productivity is higher than a pure physical retailer's *because* intent is built online first.
- **Product**: studded 57%; entry-price-point recalibration via redesign (new techniques giving more strength with less gold) plus selective 14-karat, not karatage alone.
- **Manufacturing**: ~95% in-house. The stated rationale is **design defensibility, not margin** — in a vendor ecosystem "your designs eventually get dissipated, get commoditized, get stocked with small tweaks in different stores across different brands."
- **Lab-grown diamonds: a non-event for this business.** Solitaire exposure (where LGD actually competes) is **<1% of revenue**, so BlueStone "never saw the first shift or the second shift."

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body: India - domestic jewellery retail, omnichannel across Tier 1/2/3 cities (340 stores across 134 cities)

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not applicable (retail). The pipeline proxy is the store network — 352 stores, ~20% p.a. distribution CAGR, larger (~4,500 sq ft) formats in Tier-2/3 where rent per sq ft is lower, giving greater frontage at similar absolute rent per store.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue: ~₹12,000cr in the next four years** (from ₹2,440cr in FY26) — the anchor number, restated three times.
- **SSSG ~30% over the next four years** — but critically, this is **"SSSG even at maturity," not reported SSSG**; reported SSSG will run higher because of first-year stores on a low base. Management conceded the analyst's arithmetic that 30% SSSG + 20% distribution ≠ 50% revenue CAGR on a reported basis.
- **Distribution growth ~20% CAGR (store count) over four years**, to be delivered through this year as well — store adds should **not** be read linearly quarter to quarter.
- **Operating EBITDA margin: 7.5% → "the 15% handle" over the next four years**, with the *bigger chunk* of that coming from **scale (marketing + corporate cost dilution), not store-level profitability**.
- **Marketing spend: 6.6% (FY26) → ~4.5–4.6% over the next five years**; this full year should print **below 6.6%**.
- **Blended inventory turn → ~1.7–1.8** over the next four years; "this year inventory turn should get better," improving each year.
- **Store-level ROIC ~40%** at mature inventory turns — already demonstrated by older stores, which are *still* delivering SSSG in line with or better than company average.
- **Hedge policy unchanged: ~50% of gold inventory hedged** (GML included as a hedging instrument); explicitly **not** a function of the gold price view.
- No 9-karat launch planned currently; 14-karat experiments continue at lower price points.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Customer ageing as the growth engine**: acquisition happens at age 28–32 at low ticket; the same customer at 45–50 buys ₹4–6 lakh products. The stated corollary is that BlueStone must **grow its selection upward as the base ages** — repeat AOV is already 20–30% above new.
- **Tier-2/3 densification** with larger-frontage stores at comparable absolute rent, used partly as billboard/advertising surface.
- **Non-wedding everyday jewellery** — framed as the segment "the industry overlooked for a very long time" and the deliberate positioning choice.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's 'Consumer Renaissance' - a demographic and social shift from large joint-family, price-sensitive, unorganised buying toward nuclear-family, convenience-led, organised-retail/e-commerce consumption, with rising female workforce participation and urban sprawl into Tier 2/3 cities - underpins domestic consumption demand
- India's e-commerce market is expected to expand at a 20-25% CAGR through 2029, with digital channels shifting from a transactional medium to the primary point of product discovery, favouring digital-first, omnichannel brands
- The Indian jewellery sector is shifting structurally from an occasional, wedding-led, pure-gold purchase pattern toward a 'lifestyle consumer' pattern with daily-wear, diamond and studded/14k-18k gold demand growing faster than wedding-led gold demand
- Southern India remains the largest regional demand pocket (41% of demand, plain-gold/temple designs) while Northern and Western India show higher propensity for lightweight studded jewellery, and daily-wear/occasion-led demand is rising across all regions
- Rising disposable incomes and urbanisation in Tier 2/Tier 3+ cities are converting a still largely unorganised jewellery/general-trade market (82% unorganised) toward organised, value-added retail channels
- Company-specific: a sharp, unprecedented rise in gold prices during the year caused the demand-driven inventory system to unintentionally thin out entry-level/affordable price points, weighing on new-consumer acquisition before the entry-level portfolio was redesigned and growth recovered above 30% by Q4 exit

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- The margin story is deliberately relocated: **do not look at gross margin** (product-mix noise), **look at contribution margin** (captures cost of production/manufacturing and direct costs) — which is "reasonably stable" — **and then at operating leverage**.
- Of the ~650bps of operating-leverage expansion in the last year, **the bigger chunk came from scale (corporate + marketing dilution), not store-level profit expansion**. Management used this to rebut the suggestion that slower expansion would deliver margin sooner: "that base assumption itself is flawed."
- Rent grew 35% vs 25.5% area growth; management's answer is that per-store economics (absolute rent, revenue, cost per store) are the right unit and are stable — larger Tier-2/3 stores are not "operational square feet," and lease escalation is **3–5% p.a.**
- **GMROI has declined from ~62% (FY23) to ~48% (FY26)** — management's explanation is mathematical, not structural: heavy new-store addition (young cohorts dilute turns) plus gold-price inflation on the balance-sheet date. Mature cohorts already run **1.8–2.0x** inventory turns.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- **Hedging is a risk-management policy, not a view**: ~50% of gold inventory hedged, designed around liquidity, capital structure and P&L impact. Unchanged despite gold stabilising. GML counts within the 50%.
- Inventory ₹2,800cr is the dominant capital deployment; the stated path to better ROCE runs through **inventory turn improving to 1.7–1.8** as the store base ages, not through inventory reduction.
- Marketing spend rises in absolute terms every year but falls as a % of revenue — an explicit, ongoing reallocation toward market share.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: BlueStone is an asset-light omnichannel jewellery retailer expanding via store network additions rather than manufacturing capacity build-out. The distribution footprint expanded to 340 stores across 134 cities as at 31 March 2026, with 65 new store additions during the year, balanced between new and existing geographies and between mall and high-street formats; more than half of the store network is less than three years old, which management flags as a structural tailwind as these stores mature. During the year the Company also opened two dedicated stores in the Men's and Kids category, a largely underserved format it intends to continue expanding. For FY27, management has flagged plans to significantly increase the retail footprint further, with a strategic focus on driving both store density in existing markets and geographic expansion across city tiers.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- High vertical integration - over 95% of jewellery manufactured in-house, enabling faster design-to-market cycles, responsiveness to demand shifts and control over quality
- Digital-first discovery engine - nearly 300 million online sessions in the year used as a demand-signal/design feedback loop feeding in-house manufacturing and omnichannel selling
- High repeat-purchase base - 54.5% of FY26 revenue came from repeat customers, indicating loyalty/brand trust versus one-off occasion purchases
- Store-maturity compounding - older stores show improving economics over time as local brand recognition and repeat custom build, distinct from occasion-led retail formats
- Highest revenue growth among leading jewellery retail peers in the period while maintaining gross margins

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Group structure] The company is "Formerly Known as BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle Private Limited" (CIN L72900KA2011PLC059678) and reports both standalone and consolidated results; the consolidated P&L carries a "Share of loss of investments accounted for using the equity method" and a Non-Controlling Interest, indicating subsidiaries/associates that the deck does not otherwise describe.
- [Reporting basis] Every headline slide, operating metric and databook table is labelled "Standalone"; only the annexure P&L statements present the Consolidated entity, so headline metrics should not be read as group figures.
- [Leadership] Gaurav Singh Kushwaha is Chairman, MD and CEO (prior: Amazon; IIT Delhi); the board includes independent directors Rajesh Kumar Dahiya, Rohit Bhasin and Neha Kant, and non-executive nominee directors Sameer Dileep Nath (360One, Citi) and Prashanth Prakash (Accel India), i.e. investor nominees on the board.
- [Milestone] "Digital Milestone: 1M+ Instagram Followers" and "Top 3 jewellery retailers in India by Instagram followers (May 2025)".
- [Data caveat] The timeline slide states the online retail channel "expanded to cover 12,600 PIN codes" while the glance slide states "12,660+ PIN codes serviced (Jun '26)"; both readings are recorded rather than reconciled.
